text:
Can you write the pitch for our crowdfunding campaign? I chair the volunteer group trying to reopen the one-screen cinema in our town of 6,500. It closed in 2022.

Facts:
- We need $85,000 to replace the projector and sound system and fix the roof. The building's owner has agreed to rent it to us for $1 a year for 10 years if we raise it.
- We ran a campaign 3 years ago for $120,000. It reached $47,000 and we refunded everyone.
- This time a local bank has pledged $25,000 if we raise the rest by June 30.
- 46 volunteers have signed up to run the box office and the snack bar.
- When it closed, the cinema was selling about 180 tickets a week.
- The nearest other cinema is 38 miles away.

Keep it under 350 words.

Before I draft, here's how I'd build the case, plus some questions. Your answers will change what the pitch leads with.

**The argument as I see it**

- **Claim:** Give now, because this time the cinema can reopen.
- **Grounds:** With the bank's $25,000, the community needs to raise $60,000, which is half of last time's $120,000 target. The last campaign raised $47,000, so we need $13,000 more than people have already shown they'll give. There's also a $1-a-year lease for 10 years, 46 volunteers already signed up, 180 tickets a week when it closed, and the next cinema is 38 miles away.
- **Link from facts to ask:** The town has already shown it will give nearly this much. The cost is lower and the plan is firmer, so the gap is small enough to close.
- **Backing:** The bank's pledge and the owner's lease mean two outside parties have already committed.
- **What a sceptic will raise:** "You failed last time." "It closed once. Why won't it close again?" "What if you miss June 30?"
- **How sure we can sound:** Firm about the target. On whether the cinema will last, we can only be as firm as your answers to question 3 allow.

**Questions**

1. **Why did the last campaign fall short, and what's different now?** Was the $1 lease new? Was the $120,000 for a different plan? This is the first thing past donors will wonder about.
2. **What happens to the money if you miss June 30?** Is it all-or-nothing with refunds again? Does the bank pledge disappear? Your refund last time is a reason to trust you, and I'd like to use it.
3. **How will the cinema pay its running costs once it's open?** I mean film rental, utilities and insurance. Do you have a ticket price, a rough budget, or a weekly break-even number? The closure in 2022 is the main doubt about whether it can last.
4. **Why did it close in 2022?** If the reason no longer applies (for example the old operator retired, or the rent is now $1), that's a strong answer to that doubt.
5. **Rewards for backers?** For example tickets, a named seat, or a founding membership. Tell me the tiers if you have them.
6. **Names:** the cinema's name, the group's name, who signs, and the campaign link or platform.

Skip any you don't know. I'll write around the gaps and won't make anything up.

1. I don't know exactly why it fell short. What's different: the goal is $35,000 lower, and the bank's $25,000 counts toward it, so we need $60,000 from the public. Three local businesses have also already pledged $11,000 in writing. I don't know if the lease or plan was different last time.
2. All-or-nothing. If we don't reach $85,000 by June 30, every pledge is returned in full.
3. I don't know. No budget or break-even number yet.
4. I don't know.
5. No tiers yet.
6. The Majestic on Main Street. I'm Ruth Albers, the chair, and I'll sign it. I don't have the group name or platform to give you.

<final_document>
**Bring the Majestic back**

The Majestic on Main Street has been dark since 2022. When it closed, it was still selling about 180 tickets a week. Since then, the nearest cinema has been 38 miles away, a 76-mile round trip for a night at the movies.

We can reopen it. We need $85,000 to replace the projector and sound system and to fix the roof. If we raise that, the building's owner will rent the Majestic to us for $1 a year for ten years.

$36,000 of it is already pledged. A local bank has promised $25,000 if we raise the rest by June 30, and three local businesses have pledged $11,000 in writing. That leaves $49,000 to come from the rest of us.

Many of you will remember that we've tried this before. Three years ago we set out to raise $120,000 and reached $47,000. That wasn't enough, so we returned every dollar. This time the goal is $35,000 lower, and the bank and three businesses are already committed. The $49,000 still needed is only $2,000 more than this town gave last time. Split across our 6,500 residents, it comes to about $7.50 each.

The same promise holds. It's all or nothing. If we don't reach $85,000 by June 30, every pledge will be returned in full.

We're also planning beyond opening night. Forty-six volunteers have already signed up to run the box office and the snack bar, and the rent will be $1 a year.

If we fall short, the bank's pledge and the $1 lease both go, the screen stays dark, and the closest movie stays 38 miles away.

Please pledge today, and ask a neighbour to do the same.

Ruth Albers
Chair, the volunteer group to reopen the Majestic
</final_document>

The pitch is about 300 words. Please check these before you post it:

- **The $49,000 figure is my assumption.** I took it that the businesses' $11,000 counts toward the $60,000 you need from the public, which leaves $49,000. The "$2,000 more than last time" and "$7.50 each" lines depend on that. If the $11,000 is extra on top of the $60,000, tell me and I'll rewrite those lines.
- **Running costs are the weak spot.** A reader who wonders whether the Majestic can last once it reopens has only the volunteers and the $1 rent as an answer. I didn't say it will break even because you have no figures yet. Once you have even a rough monthly budget, adding it would make the pitch noticeably stronger.
- **I didn't say why the last campaign fell short or why the cinema closed,** because you don't know. If someone finds out, one sentence on each would help.
- **Gaps to fill:** your group's name in the signature, the platform link, and reward tiers if you add any. I also left the year off June 30. If the page might still be read after next summer, add "2027."
